Skeleton Screen

The skeletal screen is a blank version of the page. It is usually outlined by some gray blocks before the page is fully rendered. After the data is loaded, it is replaced with the real content.

The skeleton screen mechanism is provided by the Mini Program framework. This mechanism can be used to load the skeleton screen earlier than the skeleton screen created in the service. This mechanism can reduce the white screen waiting time of users and bring better user experience.

To facilitate development, the developer tool provides the capability of automatically generating skeleton screen code. The skeleton screen can be generated based on the developer's configuration.

Skeleton Screen Compiling

There are two ways to compile the skeleton screen: automatic generation and manual development. Automatic generation is simple and efficient, and manual development is more flexible. After automatic generation, developers can manually modify it. Developers can flexibly select it according to their own requirements. The skeleton screen depends on the template file. The following describes the skeleton screen template SK file in detail.

SK file

The SK file is the template file of the frame skeleton screen. The file is named *.sk and consists of template and style.

The template tag is the standard HTML subset. Only the div tag and the id, class, and style attributes are supported. style is the standard CSS.

The sample code is as follows:

<template>
  <!--  Skeleton screen HTML code, standard HTML subset; Only the `div` tag and the `id`, `class`, and `style` attributes are supported -->
  <div id="sk-main" class="sk-container">
    <div class="sk_6_2_5_46" style="height: 2.7287%; width: 6.8792%; top: 5.4575%;"></div>
  </div>
</template>
<style>
  /* Skeleton screen style code, standard CSS */
  .sk_6_2_5_46 {
    background-image: linear-gradient(transparent 0%, #efefef 0%, #efefef 100%, transparent 0%) !important;
    background-size: 100% 1.6rem;
    background-repeat: 'repeat-y' !important;
    position: fixed !important;
  }
</style>

Auto Generated

1.Developers can use the developer tool to generate skeleton screen code for the page that is being previewed. The generation button entry is located in the selection list at the lower left corner of the simulator panel.

2.Click Generate Skeleton to generate the Skeleton configuration in the app.json file. The generated configuration is as follows:

"skeleton": { "page": { "page/tabbar/component/index": "page/tabbar/component/index.sk" } }

3.After you click this button, a *.sk file is generated in the directory at the same level on the current page（* indicates the page name）. The file contains the code template and style of the skeleton screen. Developers can modify and adjust the file.

Manual development

Developers can create and compile *.sk files anywhere in the Mini Program project, depending on the preceding skeleton screen template.

Generating Configurations

Attribute Name Type Default value Mandatory or Not Description
loading String spin no Animation displayed on the skeleton screen. The following enumerated values are supported: spin, chiaroscuro, shine
image Object {shape:'rect', color:'#efefef'} no This configuration accepts 2 fields，color、shape。color and shape are used to determine the color and shape of the picture blocks in the skeleton page，The color supports only hexadecimal, and the shape supports two enumerated values，circle and rect
button Object {color:'#efefef'} no This configuration receives one field color. color is used to determine the color that is considered a button block in the skeleton page
backgroundColor String '#fff' no Background color of the skeleton screen

Display Control

The display of the skeleton screen needs to be configured in ["skeleton"]["page"] in the app.json file. The configuration example is the same as the preceding configuration example. The skeleton configuration file app.json provides the skeleton screen display configuration in the Mini Program global configuration file. The rules are as follows:

"skeleton": {
  "page": {
   "page/tabbar/component/index": "page/tabbar/component/index.sk"
  }
 }

When the skeleton screen is automatically generated, the display configuration is automatically written into the configuration file. Configurations need to be manually written during manual generation.

Remove Control

The skeleton screen can be removed in two ways: timeout hiding and active hiding. Timeout hiding is controlled by configuration, which is easy to use. Active hiding is controlled by calling the API to control the hiding time more accurately. In addition, local hiding is supported to achieve the effect of progressive loading.

Timeout Hide

Without any configuration, the frame skeleton screen will be automatically hidden 2000ms after loading. You can set the global timeout interval in the ["skeleton"]["config"]["timeout"] field in the app.json file. The unit is ms. When timeout is set to 0, the global timeout hiding configuration is disabled.

"skeleton": {
  "config": {
   "timeout": 1000
  }
 }

Actively hide

After setting timeout to 0 to disable the skeleton screen timeout hiding configuration, you can use the this.removeSkeleton() API to hide the skeleton screen.

The sample code is as follows:

Page({
  onReady() {
    this.removeSkeleton && this.removeSkeleton();
  },
});

Partially hidden

You can use the this.removeSkeleton({id:''}) API to partially hide the skeleton screen node with a specified ID. The sample code is as follows:

Page({
  onReady() {
    this.removeSkeleton && this.removeSkeleton({ id: "node-id" });
  },
});

Bug & Tip

  • Tip: You can click to generate a skeleton screen only after the current page is loaded；
  • Tip: The skeleton screen only includes the visible area on the first screen of the page. For container components such as the swiper that scroll horizontally, subelements beyond the screen are ignored；
  • Tip: If the effect is not satisfactory, you are advised to adjust the related configuration to automatically generate the screen again or modify the automatically generated skeleton screen code（Each element uses absolute positioning, allowing developers to modify the element without affecting the fixed position and size of other elements）；
  • Tip: Skeleton screens are usually used on pages such as product lists and news lists. The display effect is poor on pages with many animations, native components, and complex components；
  • Tip: The generated skeleton screen code will contain the page data during preview(such as text) and will be used to fill the page；
  • Tip: If an element with a background color (backgroundColor) is directly deleted, the generated skeleton screen may not meet the expectation. Developers can change the background color of the skeleton screen module as required；
  • Tip: The skeleton screen configuration does not support configurations such as remove to handle the DOM element selected by the operation separately. To remove or hide certain elements, you can change the *.sk file.
